svg.text: Heavy metals inactivate proteins by binding cysteine sulfur
Hg²⁺, Pb²⁺, Cd²⁺ are soft metal ions; thiol sulfur is a soft base, so the bond is very tight.
Bridging two cysteines, or blocking an active-site –SH, distorts the fold and kills activity.
Metals can also displace Zn²⁺ from zinc fingers and other metal-binding sites.
None of these happen: metal salts at toxic levels neither hydrolyze the backbone,
change one amino acid into another, nor make the solution strongly basic.
